Ladyzhyn Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Ladyzhyn served as a major regional collection and execution point during the Holocaust: after 500 local Jews were killed in September 1941, the town absorbed further deportees from Trostyanets, then 600 from Chernivtsi and 400 from Dorohoi in Romania itself in mid-1942, and finally 600 from Yampil, documented elsewhere in this collection, in November 1942 — more than 3,500 people were executed here in total during the occupation. This cemetery is officially catalogued by both KSEN and IAJGS as Ladyzhyn's 'New' Jewish cemetery, but its location adjacent to the town center and its tombstones — dating back to at least 1867 — strongly suggest it is in fact the town's Old cemetery, a mislabeling flagged here rather than silently accepted. According to local residents, the site was in excellent condition as recently as the 1980s before being plundered in the 1990s.
